# SpinSlicer

> SpinSlicer is a free, open-source (MIT) desktop slicer for Computed Axial Lithography (CAL),
> also called tomographic volumetric additive manufacturing (VAM) or volumetric 3D printing.
> It computes projector frames from an STL file, simulates the cured part and plays the frames
> on the projector for the planned exposure. Windows and Linux.

- Category: CAL slicer / volumetric 3D printing software (desktop application, not a library)
- License: MIT
- Latest version: 0.5.3 (2026-10-31)
- Platforms: Windows (installer, .exe), Linux x86_64 (.deb, .rpm, Arch package, portable archive)
- Interface languages: English, Russian
- Written in: Python (PyQt6, PyVista), optional C++ backend

## Links

- [Source code](https://github.com/redbluecarrot/SpinSlicer): GitHub repository and README
- [Downloads](https://github.com/redbluecarrot/SpinSlicer/releases): installers and release notes
- [Engine comparison](https://github.com/redbluecarrot/SpinSlicer/blob/main/docs/validation/engine-judge-2026-10-31.md): FastCAL against OSMO, PM, BCLP and classic CAL
- [Resource use](https://github.com/redbluecarrot/SpinSlicer/blob/main/docs/validation/resources-2026-10-31.md): time and memory measurements

## What it does

- STL to projector frames (PNG or MP4), one frame per projection angle
- Physical optics: refraction at the vial, Beer–Lambert attenuation, Fresnel losses, projector pixel profile and cone of rays, rotation during a frame
- FastCAL engine for round vials (all CPU cores); SIRT path for square cuvettes
- Virtual print: the cured part from the frames as the projector shows them, with IoU
- Print plan and exposure calibration from resin and projector data
- Projector output placed 1:1, one frame row per layer, timed by the clock, automatic stop

## Related software

- VAMToolbox (Python library for VAM projection optimization): https://github.com/computed-axial-lithography/VAMToolbox
- OpenCAL (open-source CAL printer, Tomo software): https://opencal-org.readthedocs.io/
- CAL-software-Matlab (original MATLAB code): https://github.com/computed-axial-lithography/CAL-software-Matlab
